gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on battery power the XGIMI Vibe One gives only 64 lumens in Eco mode. That is ProjectorCentral's measurement from July 2026, against 229 lumens when plugged in. The same lab measured the XGIMI MoGo 4 at 151 to 154 lumens in Eco, 258 to 270 in Standard and about 400 in Performance.
standout_why: I compared against all three cited pages. The Hook Up (2026-10-23) measured only the Elfin Flip Plus (484 lm high-performance, 345 lm standard, 265:1 contrast, 90 min on a UGREEN power bank) and the Aurzen Zip Pro. It has nothing on the MoGo 4, Vibe One, Capsule 3 or MoGo 2 Pro. Both RTINGS list pages (under-500 and portable) gave no lumen, contrast, battery or input-lag figures in the page text I could open. Their review pages load their data with JavaScript and returned only navigation, so I could not see whether RTINGS gives battery-mode brightness. ChatGPT's answer only calls the Vibe One 'much dimmer' and gives the MoGo 4 '450 ISO lumens'. None of the pages puts measured lumens per power mode, input lag or fan noise for these battery models side by side.
decides: This confirms the MoGo 4 ($479) as the battery pick. ProjectorCentral measured 151 to 154 lm in Eco, the mode XGIMI rates for 2.5 hours, and about 400 lm in Performance. It also measured 22.1 ms input lag in Game mode, and Expert Reviews ran it 1 h 52 min in Standard mode. It weakens the Vibe One as a battery choice. Its Eco mode measured 64 lm, about a quarter of its plugged-in 229 lm, and Android Authority measured at best 96 minutes on battery. Treat the Vibe One as a $269 plug-in projector. The Capsule 3 measured 201 ANSI lm on AC (ProjectorReviews), and the reviewer says brightness drops about 40% on battery. Both are well below the MoGo 4.
